extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants to the ERC Starting Grant (early-career principal investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how ERC Starting Grant proposals and applicants will be evaluated, including the single criterion of 'Excellence', its components, and the two-step evaluation process. Covers what panels review at each step and recent (2026) changes to assessment practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence (sole evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence is the sole evaluation criterion for ERC Starting Grants and has two main components: excellence of the research project and excellence of the principal investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels primarily evaluate the ground‑breaking nature and ambition of the project. All assessments should be made with 'Excellence' as the single overriding standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the Research Project
rubrics_metrics.description: The research project is assessed for its ground‑breaking nature, ambition, and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 2026, feasibility is no longer assessed at Step 1; Part I of the Scientific Proposal should not include details on the feasibility of the scientific approach but should present a convincing overall research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground‑breaking nature (of the project)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposed research is ground‑breaking—i.e., introduces major advances, novel directions, or transformative ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels primarily evaluate the ground‑breaking nature of the project alongside ambition; strong emphasis in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition (of the project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ambition of the project: the degree of challenge, scope, and transformative potential of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels primarily evaluate ambition together with ground‑breaking nature; ambition should be clear in the synopsis (Part B1) especially since Step 1 reviewers are generalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility (of the project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility of the proposed approach and plans for delivering the research outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 2026, feasibility is no longer assessed at Step 1 (synopsis stage). Feasibility may be assessed at Step 2; consequently, Part I should avoid detailed feasibility argumentation and instead present an overall convincing research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the Principal Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall assessment of the PI's excellence as reflected in intellectual capacity, creativity, and commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels evaluate the PI's personal qualities as part of the single 'Excellence' criterion; information on the CV/track record matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual capacity (of the PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI's intellectual capacity, including evidence of scholarly/technical ability and the capability to carry out the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated via CV, track record, and outputs; considered under the PI excellence component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity (of the PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI's creativity—ability to produce original ideas, approaches, and to push frontiers in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as part of PI excellence; examples of original work and novel contributions strengthen this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment (of the PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI's commitment to the project, including dedication of time and resources necessary to deliver the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via statements of commitment and CV; part of PI excellence judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑step evaluation process — Step 1 (materials and reviewer type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: panel members review only Part B1 (synopsis) and the CV. Panels at Step 1 are composed of generalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reviewers are often generalists at Step 1, the synopsis (Part B1) must present a convincing, accessible statement of ground‑breaking nature and ambition. From 2026, do not include detailed feasibility arguments in Part I since feasibility is not assessed at Step 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑step evaluation process — Step 2 (materials, interviews, specialists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2: a new panel of specialists reviews both B1 and B2 (the full description). Interviews take place at Step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed assessments including feasibility are made at Step 2; applicants should be prepared to defend methods and feasibility in interviews and the full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent external experts and access to materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels may be assisted by independent external experts working remotely; these experts have access to Part I, Part II, and the proposed budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External experts may contribute specialist input during review; budget and full proposal details can be seen by those experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel structure and membership selection
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 28 panels across three domains (Life Sciences; Physical and Engineering Sciences; Social Sciences and Humanities). Each panel has a chair and 10–16 members. Panel members are selected by the ERC Scientific Council based on their scientific reputation, and the majority may be generalists rather than specialists in the specific area(s) of a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many panel members may be generalists, proposals (especially Part B1) should be written to be understandable and persuasive to non‑specialists while Step 2 will involve specialist reviewers.
